findings.passage: Voting should be easy and secure and our elections should reflect the will of the electorate, not ideologues.
findings.note: Statement on his 2026 re-election campaign about page. It does not mention ID or citizenship proof.

findings.passage: As our state representative, I have focused on making health care more affordable and accessible, investing in public education and our first responders, protecting reproductive rights, passing gun safety legislation, and preserving ballot access and respect for our election results regardless of their outcome.
findings.note: Campaign about page lists preserving ballot access among his focus areas.

findings.passage: Yes. Fundamental to our democracy is that every eligible voter should be able to access the ballot box, accepting that our current elections are free and fair, and that the results of our elections are respected regardless of outcome. I strongly believe no-excuse mail-in voting is critical to meet these tenets. I additionally believe that we should enact early in-person voting, same-day registration, open primaries, pre-registration of those eligible 16-year olds and above so that they are on voter rolls when they turn 18, and independent, non-partisan redistricting.
findings.note: His written answer in the WESA candidate survey to the question 'Do you support no-excuse mail-in voting in Pennsylvania — yes/no?'. It supports no-excuse mail voting and other access measures; it does not address ID.
